history.summary: An archaeological ruin site, not an active full temple (though it draws pilgrims and worship continues at the site); a Hindu/Shakta temple complex generally attributed to the Chutia kings of the 13th-14th century, with the cultural period of the remains placed between the 10th and 14th centuries. Excavations in 1968-1971 unearthed a granite (Asmamayai) temple plinth with sculptures of Indra on Airavata, Surya on a chariot, Kartikeya, Ganesha and a huge Nandi bull; the chief deity is identified with Durga in her Shakti form (Kechai-Khaiti, a tribal goddess served by Deori priests). The Krishna-Rukmini 'Malini' garland legend was implanted on the site by Srimanta Sankardev in the 16th century. Dating conflict: most sources say 13th-14th century; some travel sources say 14th-15th. CSV town 'Malinithan' is the site name, not a town; corrected to the nearest town, Likabali (about 1 km west).

name: Malinithan Temple Ruins
town_description: Likabali is a small town in Lower Siang district on the Assam-Arunachal border, about 1 km west of the Malinithan archaeological site and its nearest administrative centre. A gateway between the Assam plains and the Siang hills, it serves pilgrims and visitors heading to the Malinithan ruins and the nearby Akashiganga stream.

travel.airport: Lilabari Airport (North Lakhimpur, Assam) or Dibrugarh Airport, Assam
travel.road: By bus or car from Guwahati (Assam) or Itanagar; about 1 km east of Likabali

visitor_information.opening_hours: No published timings; visit during daylight hours
